source_verification_receipts.locator: PDF p. 5, §3.1.2, Theorems 3.5-3.6 and proof of Theorem 3.6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3.5 generically identifies the effect using the first k(l) cumulants; Theorem 3.6 states nonidentification through order three for l=1. Its proof says it parameterizes the model, computes the vanishing ideal of the modified parametrization, computes a reduced Gröbner basis in an elimination order, and finds the effect as a root of a degree-two polynomial.
The one-latent-component calculation uses covariance together with fourth-order cumulants under zero-mean and unit-variance normalization; it is not a third-cumulant-only unknown-chain inverse.

The paper defines constraints via elimination of a polynomial parametrization and states that an elimination-order reduced Gröbner basis contains the lowest-degree parameter relation; a higher-degree relation alone yields at most that many generic candidates and need not itself settle identifiability.
